lines.text: Your experience.
Employers prefer someone with experience [ervaring].
That person can work independently [zelfstandig] sooner.
Experience can come from your own country or from the Netherlands, from an internship during your studies, or from volunteer work.
What are you good at?
It is important that you have the competencies [competenties] for the work.
A competency is something you are good at.
A competency fits your character [karakter] or you have learned it — during a study programme, while working, or through a hobby.

Different kinds of work need different competencies: if you work in construction, you must be physically [fysiek] strong; if you work in healthcare [gezondheidszorg], you must be social [sociaal] and caring [zorgzaam].
Competencies involve: knowing, being able to, being and wanting.
What do you enjoy?
You can choose from different sectors [sectoren], for example: healthcare, construction, hospitality [horeca] (hotels/restaurants/cafés), education, the green sector.
If you enjoy your work and are good at it, you are also motivated [gemotiveerd].
Motivation makes your work less hard, and an employer also looks at your motivation [motivatie] during a job application.
When are you available?
An employer also asks about your availability [beschikbaarheid]: when and how much can you work?
Some jobs are fulltime [voltijd]: then you work the whole week, on average 38 hours.
You can also work parttime [deeltijd], for example two or three days.

Some jobs (for example in an office) have regular [regelmatige] working hours; other jobs (for example in hospitality) have irregular [onregelmatige] working hours — often in the evening or at the weekend.
The situation in your region.
The opportunities to work are not the same everywhere.
In a city there are often more jobs; in the Randstad there are many opportunities.
Is your job far away?
Then you must travel or perhaps move.
